note:
German Democratic Republic (East Germany) (GDR) had an embargo imposed on them from West Germany on coffee during the cold war. GDR mostly got by with importing and family connections for personal mail imports for coffee (article claims 1/5 is from family sending coffee through post).

The oil crisis and USA's loss of Vietnam war made coffee scarce and opened up a region that was more conducive to coffee bean growth. GDR invested heavily in coffee production in Vietnam but fell before the investment paid off (1990s started exporting in earnest but GDR fell that same year).

Because of the Vietnam war with USA, there was a shortage of men and women were incorporated into the workforce, with a focus on equality.

Vietnam's coffee trade is $3B+/year now.

Other discussion talks about how relationships between GDR citizens and Vietnamese citizens was highly discouraged, including claims of deportation and coerced abortion.
